title: I made this game in ~5 days with Opus + GPT -- tried to see how far an “almost 100% AI” workflow can actually go
author: No_Emphasis_2904
selftext:
I spent around **5 days** making this game.

I know that saying something is “100% AI” definitely isn’t a sign of quality, so my goal was to find out: **how much quality can I actually squeeze out of AI?**

The main setup was **Opus 5.5 + GPT**.

GPT was mostly responsible for **image generation / concept art**, while Opus handled basically everything else: **game logic, 3D models, shaders, sound, optimization, UI, balancing, implementation, etc.**

My own role was mostly coming up with the original idea, testing things, giving feedback, approving the first concept-art direction, and deciding what was good enough to keep.

I actually posted about the game earlier while it was still in development, you can find that post in my profile if you want a more detailed breakdown of the process.

In my previous post I said that the **water shader was mine**. Well... not anymore.

By the final build, Opus had completely rewritten it while optimizing the game to maintain around **60 FPS even on relatively weak phones**. The mobile version is capped to 30 FPS by default right now, but that's beside the point :)

For the promotional video in this post, I had a **separate repository with two Opus agents working on it**. One agent was creating the video, while the second one was essentially acting as an critic and reviewing what the first one produced.

Another thing that worked surprisingly well was using **scripts to validate AI work**.

For example, when I was trying to get the in-game visuals closer to AI-generated reference images, I had Opus write scripts that objectively compared different aspects of the results. You can tell it what is important to compare, and it can build its own validation pipeline around that.

I’d strongly recommend this approach in general. Giving an AI agent **tools to verify its own output** improved the quality much more than just repeatedly telling it “make it closer to the reference” (tested, 'make it closer' doesn't work, validation script works).

There was still a lot of iteration, failed attempts and manual approval involved, but overall I was pretty surprised by how far the workflow could go in only a few days, planning to set up AI QA as well.

You can play the current build here:

[**https://playgama.com/game/pirate-raid?clid=p\_3f1a7d88-5be8-4527-befb-65ad76b6b550**](https://playgama.com/game/pirate-raid?clid=p_3f1a7d88-5be8-4527-befb-65ad76b6b550)

If anyone is interested in **how a specific part was made** \-- 3D assets, shaders, AI workflow, agent setup, optimization, the promo video, etc. -- ask in the comments. Happy to explain anything.
